title: Design System: Sri Rahul Namana, Portfolio

display.purpose: The name on the title page only; uppercase.

statement.purpose: About trait words and the coda headline.

headline.purpose: Section titles, sentence case with a full stop, balanced wrap.

title.purpose: Role, client, score-page and practice names.

figure.purpose: Numbers that are facts, always followed by an Old Standard italic gloss.

body.purpose: Section subs, descriptions and card copy (46-66ch).

score.purpose: Old Standard italic: part names, years, lyrics, glosses, folios, bar numbers.

score-lead.purpose: Old Standard italic: the instrumentation line and the coda sub.

tempo.purpose: Old Standard 700 roman: the tempo marking at the head of a system and rest counts.

shadows.name: pencil-lift-hover
shadows.purpose: Primary pencil button on hover, with a 2px rise.

shadows.name: pencil-lift-on-ink
shadows.purpose: Pencil button on the ink coda.

shadows.name: sheet-on-stand
shadows.purpose: A score page on the Work stand.

shadows.name: header-rule
shadows.purpose: The running header's hairline once the page scrolls.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing for transitions and reveals; exponential ease-out, never bounce or elastic.

motion.name: linear-read
motion.purpose: Playheads reading a staff and scrubbed scroll timelines.

motion.name: staff-draw
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 0.8-1.4s ease-out, staggered 60-120ms per line or cell
motion.purpose: Staves and pencil rings draw in from the left.

motion.name: note-strike
motion.purpose: A note struck by the playhead or the pointer; head, stem and lyric turn pencil and a ripple ring opens.

motion.name: mark-stamp
motion.purpose: A rehearsal letter stamps in and fills pencil.

motion.name: heading-ink-in
motion.value: word or line translateY(105%) to 0, 0.9-1.1s ease-out
motion.purpose: Headings rise out of a clipped line box.

motion.name: block-sweep
motion.value: clip-path inset left to right with a 2px pencil scan line, 1s ease-out, 90ms stagger

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Everything honours prefers-reduced-motion; loops stop, pins fall back, the 3D scene holds.

components.name: Pencil Button
components.description: The one primary action per context; blue pencil fill, plate corners, lifts on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-pencil { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 15px 22px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--pencil, #2b46d9); color: #fff; font: 600 16px/1 var(--f-sans, 'Schibsted Grotesk', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif); letter-spacing: 0.005em; text-decoration: none; box-shadow: 0 10px 20px -14px rgba(18, 19, 23, 0.5); transition: transform .35s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), background .25s, box-shadow .35s; } .ds-btn-pencil:hover { background: var(--pencil-2, #1f36b3); transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 16px 26px -16px rgba(18, 19, 23, 0.55); } .ds-btn-pencil:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-btn-pencil:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--pencil, #2b46d9); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Line Button
components.description: Secondary action: ink text on a 1.5px ink rule that turns pencil on hover.
components.html: See the record
components.css: .ds-btn-line { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 12px 2px 10px; font: 600 16px/1 var(--f-sans, 'Schibsted Grotesk', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif); color: var(--ink, #121317); text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 1.5px solid var(--ink, #121317); transition: color .25s, border-color .25s; } .ds-btn-line:hover { color: var(--pencil, #2b46d9); border-color: var(--pencil, #2b46d9); } .ds-btn-line:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--pencil, #2b46d9); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.description: Outbound links on a score page (GitHub, Live demo, IEEE paper).

components.name: Running Header Links
components.description: Second-ink links; the current section gets a hand-drawn pencil underline.
components.html: AboutCareerWorkContact
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 28px; background: var(--paper, #eef0ec); padding: 20px 24px; } .ds-nav a { position: relative; display: inline-block; padding: 8px 0; font: 500 15px/1 var(--f-sans, 'Schibsted Grotesk', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif); color: var(--ink-2, #3d4149); text-decoration: none; transition: color .25s; } .ds-nav a:hover, .ds-nav a.is-active { color: var(--ink, #121317); } .ds-nav a svg { position: absolute; left: -3%; bottom: -3px; width: 106%; height: 8px; overflow: visible; } .ds-nav a svg path { fill: none; stroke: var(--pencil, #2b46d9); stroke-width: 2.4; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-dasharray: 1; } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--pencil, #2b46d9); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.css: .ds-page { width: min(470px, 78vw); padding: 26px 26px 18px; background: var(--sheet, #f8f9f6); border: 1px solid var(--rule, rgba(18, 19, 23, 0.14)); border-radius: 3px; box-shadow: 0 30px 60px -40px rgba(18, 19, 23, 0.5); transition: box-shadow .6s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1); } .ds-page:hover { box-shadow: 0 44px 80px -44px rgba(18, 19, 23, 0.6); } .ds-page header { text-align: center; padding-bottom: 12px; margin-bottom: 14px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, rgba(18, 19, 23, 0.14)); } .ds-page h3 { margin: 0; font: 800 24px/1.15 'Schibsted Grotesk', sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #121317; } .ds-page .cat { margin: 6px 0 0; font: italic 400 16px/1.3 'Old Standard TT', serif; color: #5b606a; } .ds-page .fig { height: 160px; border: 1px solid rgba(18, 19, 23, 0.14); background: #e4e7e1; } .ds-page .stat { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 10px; margin: 14px 0 0; } .ds-page .stat b { font: 800 30px/1 'Schibsted Grotesk', sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #121317; } .ds-page .stat i { font: italic 400 16.5px/1.2 'Old Standard TT', serif; color: #3d4149; } .ds-page .desc { margin: 10px 0 0; font: 400 15.5px/1.6 'Schibsted Grotesk', sans-serif; color: #3d4149; } .ds-page .folio { margin: 12px 0 0; text-align: center; font: italic 400 15px/1 'Old Standard TT', serif; color: #5b606a; }

components.name: Rehearsal Letter
components.description: A career role's boxed letter; stamps in and fills pencil when its role is reached.
components.css: .ds-reh { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; min-width: 30px; height: 30px; padding: 0 6px; border: 2px solid var(--ink, #121317); background: var(--paper, #eef0ec); color: var(--ink, #121317); font: 800 16px/1 'Schibsted Grotesk', sans-serif; transition: background .4s, color .4s, border-color .4s; } .ds-reh.is-lit, .ds-reh:hover { background: var(--pencil, #2b46d9); border-color: var(--pencil, #2b46d9); color: #fff; animation: ds-stamp .55s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1); } @keyframes ds-stamp { 0% { transform: scale(1.7) rotate(-12deg); } 100% { transform: none; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-reh { animation: none !important; } }

components.name: Staff with Struck Note
components.description: Five staff lines, a note that turns pencil and is struck on hover, with an English lyric below.
components.html: voice agents
components.css: .ds-staff { display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; cursor: pointer; } .ds-staff .st line { stroke: rgba(18, 19, 23, 0.4); stroke-width: 1; } .ds-staff .note { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 50% 100%; } .ds-staff .note ellipse { fill: #121317; transition: fill .25s; } .ds-staff .note line { stroke: #121317; stroke-width: 1.3; transition: stroke .25s; } .ds-staff .lyric { font: 500 14.5px/1.3 'Schibsted Grotesk', sans-serif; color: #3d4149; transition: color .25s; } .ds-staff:hover .note { animation: ds-strike .5s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1); } .ds-staff:hover .note ellipse { fill: #2b46d9; } .ds-staff:hover .note line { stroke: #2b46d9; } .ds-staff:hover .lyric { color: #2b46d9; } @keyframes ds-strike { 0% { transform: none; } 30% { transform: translateY(3px) scale(1.2); } 100% { transform: none; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-staff:hover .note { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The page is a printed orchestral score on cool manuscript paper, and the man it describes is the conductor. Every structural device is borrowed from engraved notation rather than from web UI: five-line staves are the dividers, barlines and a final double bar close a passage, rehearsal letters in square boxes mark the roles, a fermata holds the ending, and the score's own voice (tempo marks, part names, expression, lyrics) is set in an italic nineteenth-century serif beside a heavy modern grotesque. The one colour that does not belong to the printing is the conductor's blue pencil, laid over the score for cues, the current place, actions and facts.

Density is that of a score, not a brochure: generous vertical air between sections (150px on desktop), then tight, information-bearing systems inside them. Each section is built as its own scroll instrument (a pinned stepper, a slide-in staff that plays itself, a pinned rehearsal mark, a scrubbed spotlight, a pinned page-turning stand, a velocity ticker, a curtain with a sung cadence), and all of them speak one motion vocabulary taken from the score: staves draw, notes are struck, marks stamp, a playhead reads.

The world rejects, by thesis, the gradient hero, the card grid and the tech-logo wall. Project pages are single printed sheets on a stand, not tiles; client proof is a ruled list, not a wall of logos.
keyCharacteristics: Cool manuscript paper, near-black engraving ink, one blue pencil.
Heavy Schibsted Grotesk (800-900, tight negative tracking) for everything engraved; Old Standard TT italic for everything the score says.
Staves, barlines, rehearsal boxes, a fermata and a treble clef drawn as line-work SVG; the 3D hero is ruled from straight lines only.
Flat printed surfaces with hairline rules; the only lifted object is a score page on the stand.
English only, including every musical marking.

rules.name: The One Pencil Rule
rules.body: Blue marks only actions, the current place, cues and facts. It is never decoration, never a heading underline, never a background panel. If a blue mark cannot answer "click me", "you are here", "this is cued" or "this is a fact", it is ink.

rules.name: The Client's Own Colour Rule
rules.body: A client row may borrow that client's brand colour for its pointer wash, its sweep line, its figures on hover and its arrow disc. That colour stays inside its row and never enters the page's own system.

rules.name: The Print and the Performance Rule
rules.body: Schibsted Grotesk is the engraving; Old Standard italic is what the score says. A gloss beside a figure, a year, a part name or an expression mark is always Old Standard; a heading or a number is always Schibsted. Never set a heading in the serif or a lyric in the grotesque roman.

rules.name: The English Markings Rule
rules.body: Every musical marking is written in plain English ("With purpose", "broadening, then held", "End", "Back to top"). No Italian tempo or expression terms.

rules.name: The One Home Rule
rules.body: Each fact has one place on the page. A number that lives in Clients (99%, 55M+, client-validated) is not restated elsewhere; the title page's score ends on its peak note without the figure.

rules.name: The Staff Is the Divider Rule
rules.body: Sections and entries are separated by what a score uses: a five-line staff, a hairline, a double rule (3px double under the programme head), a barline, a final double bar. Never a card edge or a coloured band.

rules.name: The Only Paper Lifts Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "a physical sheet or a pressable pencil mark lying on the paper". Text blocks, rows, rules and sections never cast one.

dos: Do keep blue to the pencil's four jobs: actions, the current place, cues and facts.
Do set every musical marking in English, in Old Standard (italic for expression and lyrics, 700 roman for tempo).
Do give each fact one home; the 99% lives in Clients only.
Do draw motion from the score: staves draw (stroke-dashoffset), notes are struck, rehearsal marks stamp, a 2px pencil playhead reads, headings ink in word by word.
Do ease every transition with the exponential ease-out `cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)`; linear timing only for playheads and scrubbed scroll.
Do animate transform, opacity and clip-path (stroke-dashoffset for line drawing); pause every loop off screen and on hidden tabs.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion` everywhere: transitions collapse, loops stop, the 3D scene holds, pinned sequences fall back to plain reveals, and rings and staves are shown drawn.
Do give each new section its own scroll structure, built from a score device.
Do show stock project art as a grayscale printed plate and a real screenshot in colour when its page is current.
donts: Don't put a pencil underline under a section heading; headings are ink only.
Don't use Italian score terms (no "con brio", "tutti", "fine", "D.C."), or any non-English text.
Don't repeat a number across sections (99%, 55M+, client-validated live in Clients).
Don't use bounce, elastic or overshoot easing.
Don't build a gradient hero, a card grid or a tech-logo wall; project pages are sheets on a stand, clients are ruled rows.
Don't add shadows to text, rows or sections; only a sheet on the stand or the pencil button lifts.
Don't add a second accent colour; a client's brand colour stays inside its own row.
Don't add small labels above section titles; a section opens with its headline.
